provider: hop.js CDN (cdn.hopjs.net) — Bunny.net's free OSS mirror of npm + cdnjs

free_tier.stated: A free CDN for open source projects; the home and about pages state no storage quota.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: A file of 64,458,752 bytes answers HTTP 200 (HEAD, declared Content-Length); no per-file cap is stated on the home or about pages.
per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: Every package is permanently distributed across Bunny Storage’s globally deployed SSD regions.

egress.terms: Described as a free CDN for open source projects; the home and about pages state no traffic limit or price.

tooling: Plain HTTPS GET: https://cdn.hopjs.net/npm/<pkg>@<ver>/<path>. No auth. Drop-in for any HTTP client / rclone http remote / curl. NOTE the path form carries the version twice when the mirror rewrites you, and the un-versioned form 302s to a broken URL. Always pin <pkg>@<ver> explicitly.
chaining: This is the missing piece for the npm-as-storage chain: publish the blob to npm (email-only identity), then serve it from hop.js instead of jsDelivr and the 50 MB jsDelivr file cap stops applying. Publish a 64 MB shard per npm version, chain thousands of versions, serve all of them free with no bandwidth ceiling. Because the mirror is permanent and Bunny-hosted, an npm unpublish does not remove the served copy in the short term.

limits.value: no per-file cap stated; a 64,458,752-byte file is served

limits_note: Per-object-cap: ~64 MB proven, likely bounded by npm's own ~100 MB tarball publish limit rather than by hop.js. cache-write-gated: only packages already in the npm/cdnjs index are mirrored. You cannot upload to hop.js directly, you publish upstream. /gh/ (GitHub) paths are not supported (404).
reliability_note: Young third-party service (Bunny-backed, 119 PoPs, logging disabled by design). Single point of failure with no SLA; for a 1 TiB/day workload you would mirror across hop.js + unpkg + jsDelivr so one going away is not an outage. Sustained single-stream measured 11.3 MB/s vs jsDelivr's 6.4 MB/s on the same 32 MB object.

extras.verified_at_basis: re-checked against the first-party page on 2026-11-19 (a verify run); evidence rows dated by the seed pass, which ended 2026-10-21, keep that date as an upper bound
extras.quota_verbatim: No quota of its own. It is a permanent mirror: every file is copied into Bunny Storage SSD and served from there, so your ceiling is the npm cap. Probed single files of 32.2 MB, 54.0 MB and 64.5 MB — all served complete and byte-identical to the unpkg copy (sha256 match on the 53,974,528-byte .node and the 64,458,752-byte .exe). No per-file cap was hit at any size tried.

extras.egress_verbatim: Free and unmetered — it is a free public CDN; no account, no key, no billing surface at all. Origin->CDN transit is Bunny's own storage, so there is no origin bill either.

Publish a 64 MB shard per npm version, chain thousands of versions, serve all of them free with no bandwidth ceiling. Because the mirror is permanent and Bunny-hosted, an npm unpublish does not remove the served copy in the short term.

NOTE the path form carries the version twice when the mirror rewrites you, and the un-versioned form 302s to a broken URL — always pin <pkg>@<ver> explicitly.
extras.agent_focus: CDN / edge platforms as storage+egress: Fastly (free tier + Fast Forward OSS), Akamai/Linode, Bunny.net (storage + free origin->CDN transit), KeyCDN, CacheFly, Gcore, CDN77, StackPath status, Edgio/Limelight status, jsDelivr, unpkg, esm.sh, Statically, raw.githack, ghproxy mirrors. Question asked: which CDN gives free or near-free egress so a cheap origin becomes viable. Cloudflare R2 excluded per brief. Hard-probed every per-file cap with real GETs this session.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
